name: Pioneer 11
best_known_for: First spacecraft to encounter Saturn — flew past Jupiter in 1974 then used the Jupiter gravity assist to reach Saturn in 1979, 22 years before Cassini
credit: Spin-stabilised RTG-powered probe (~259 kg), sibling of Pioneer 10 with the same bus + Pioneer Plaque message-to-the-stars. Launched 1973-04-06 on Atlas SLV-3D Centaur D-1A + Star-37E from Cape Canaveral LC-36B. Jupiter flyby 1974-12-03 at 43 000 km — the closest of any Pioneer encounter, returned the first polar-region images and the gravity assist needed to reach Saturn. Saturn encounter 1979-09-01 at 21 000 km from the cloud tops — first detailed images of the ring system, discovery of a new ring (F-ring) and a new moon (Epimetheus rediscovery), confirmed Saturn's magnetic field aligned within 1° of its rotation axis. Continued outbound observations of the heliosphere until last contact 1995-11-24. Now ~93 AU from the Sun, headed toward the constellation Aquila; passes nearest to star Lambda Aquilae in ~4 million years.
